name: Joram (Son of King Toi of Hamat, sent to David)
title: Ambassador from Hamat to King David
summary: Joram was the son of King Toi (also called Tou) of Hamat. He was sent by his father to King David to congratulate him on his victory over Hadadezer, king of Zobah, who had been an enemy of Hamat. Joram brought gifts of gold, silver, and bronze, which David dedicated to the Lord.

keyEvents.title: Sent to David with Gifts
keyEvents.description: King Toi sent his son Joram to King David to greet him and bless him, because David had defeated Hadadezer, who had waged war against Toi.

keyEvents.title: Delivery of Precious Gifts
keyEvents.description: Joram brought items of silver, gold, and bronze as gifts for David. These represented Hamat's gratitude and desire for peace with Israel.

keyEvents.title: David's Dedication of the Gifts
keyEvents.description: King David dedicated Joram's gifts to the Lord, along with the silver and gold he had taken from other nations he had conquered.

keyEvents.title: Parallel Account in 1 Chronicles
keyEvents.description: The same event is described in 1 Chronicles, where Joram is called Hadoram. He was sent to congratulate David on his victory over Hadadezer.
